changes.text: Your "bytes-as-transmitted is the right fallback" framing matches a choice we already made for x402's own offer-receipt extension ([`offerReceiptHash`](https://github.com/holistis/tokenizen/blob/main/packages/capacity-attest/src/schema.ts) in our DeliveryClaim schema). The receipt is `{format, payload, signature}` with format `eip712` or `jws` (spec §3.1), and neither format exposes one stable canonical byte string: for eip712 the signing digest derives from normative types the spec says MUST NOT be transmitted (§3.2.1), for jws the payload is opaque base64url inside the compact serialization.

One data point for the canonical-form side, from a defect we found in our own code today. Where JCS implementations actually diverge is numbers, not member order.

Our Python canonicalizer used the language's float repr. It produced `1e-05`, `1e-07` and `1.2345678901234568e+20` where RFC 8785 requires ECMAScript `Number::toString`: `0.00001`, `1e-7`, `123456789012345680000`. A signature over such a body then fails in any other implementation. Vector 52 of the work-acceptance corpus ([maximusrufus/work-acceptance-record@6b2f730](https://github.com/maximusrufus/work-acceptance-record/tree/6b2f73

changes.author: stillmarcus24
changes.text:
@babyblueviper1 — your float finding generalises further than the three cases, and the generalisation is a problem for how this section gets validated.

RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3 doesn't describe a number format. It defers to ECMAScript `Number::toString`. So **a JavaScript implementation inherits the required behaviour from the host and cannot fail these vectors**, while every other host language has to reimplement double-to-shortest-round-trip. I measured Python's `json.dumps` against the requirement — **7 of 11 diverge, in 6 classes**:

| JSON text | required | `json.dumps` | class |
|---|---|---|-

- presign-guard-wallet's mandatePayer() makes x402 payments with the §7 binding as the EIP-3009 nonce.
- JCS bytes, digest, signature and the EIP-3009/Permit2 binding values match authority-vectors.json byte for byte.
